name: Voxel Raycasting with Vertical Slicing
definition: A raycasting technique that renders a 3D voxel grid by treating each voxel column as 12 distinct vertical layers (indexed 0-11). For each screen column, a ray is cast into the map. When a voxel is hit, the algorithm iterates through all 12 vertical indices of that voxel to draw them as stacked horizontal stripes (or vertical slices in screen space) centered around the ray's intersection point, allowing for the visualization of voxel thickness and internal structure.
